structures.label: Trapezius, middle fibers
structures.description: Horizontal middle fibers of the trapezius.

structures.label: Trapezius, lower fibers
structures.description: Lower fibers of the trapezius running up to the scapular spine.
structures.function: Pull the shoulder blades down and rotate them upwards for overhead reach.

structures.label: Latissimus dorsi
structures.description: Broad flat muscle covering the lower and mid back, inserting on the humerus.
structures.function: Pulls the arm down and back; the main muscle in pull-ups and rows.

structures.label: Rhomboids
structures.description: Rhomboid-shaped muscles between the spine and the shoulder blade.
structures.function: Retract and stabilise the shoulder blade.

structures.label: Serratus posterior superior
structures.description: Thin muscle under the rhomboids attaching to ribs 2–5.
structures.function: Assists lifting the ribs when breathing in.

structures.label: Erector spinae (thoracic)
structures.description: Three columns of muscle running along both sides of the spine.
structures.function: Extend the spine and keep the trunk upright.

structures.label: Multifidus & semispinalis
structures.description: Short deep muscles linking neighbouring vertebrae.
structures.function: Fine control and stability of each spinal segment.

structures.label: Thoracic discs
structures.description: Thin cartilage cushions between the thoracic vertebrae.
structures.function: Absorb load; the ribcage makes this the stiffest part of the spine.

structures.label: Thoracic vertebrae T1–T12
structures.description: Twelve vertebrae of the mid back, each linked to a pair of ribs.
structures.function: Protect the chest organs and allow rotation.

structures.label: Ribs
structures.description: Twelve pairs of curved bones forming the ribcage.
structures.function: Protect the heart and lungs and move with breathing.

structures.label: Scapula
structures.description: Shoulder blade, gliding over the back of the ribcage.
structures.function: Base for the shoulder; controlled by the trapezius and rhomboids.
